stem: A patient with appendicitis first has poorly localised periumbilical pain, then develops sharply localised right-lower-quadrant pain when the inflamed appendix contacts the abdominal wall. Which change explains the second phase?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This contributes to the early diffuse pain but remains poorly localised.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Somatic innervation of the parietal lining produces sharper, better-localised pain than visceral afferents.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It can contribute to visceral discomfort but does not explain the new precise abdominal-wall localisation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This would tend to refer pain to the shoulder through phrenic pathways, not the right lower quadrant.

options.label: E
options.explanation: It would affect venous drainage and does not create this characteristic temporal pain shift.

context: Visceral afferents produce diffuse midline pain; involvement of the somatically innervated abdominal lining produces precise localisation.
